name: The Restaurant at Ananda
why_it_matters: Ananda's main dining room sits inside the 100-acre Tehri-Garhwal Maharaja's Palace Estate, 1,065 m above the Ganges. The kitchen builds Ayurveda-calibrated menus around each guest's dosha — an in-house dietician sets the brief, the chef cooks to it. India's most decorated wellness retreat eats here.
insider_tip: Non-residents need to book a spa day or meal reservation in advance — gates don't open to walk-ins. Ask for the Tree Top Deck table at sunset; it cantilevers over the Sal forest with a clear line to the river valley below.
signature_address: The Palace Estate, Narendra Nagar, Tehri-Garhwal, Uttarakhand 249175

name: Neemrana's Glasshouse on the Ganges (Restaurant)
signature_dish: rustic hunter-style curry with pit-roasted meats
why_it_matters: Neemrana's Himalayan outpost on a wooded bend of the Ganges 23 km upstream of Rishikesh — a former British forest bungalow turned heritage hotel. The kitchen runs a chef-led seasonal menu pulling Tehri-Garhwal, Nepali and Himachali dishes together; meats are procured fresh, never long-frozen, and a lot of the cooking happens over an open pit.
insider_tip: It's a 45-min drive from Laxman Jhula on a single-lane mountain road — call ahead with arrival time so the chef can plan the pit roast. Day visitors can dine if they reserve, otherwise stay one night and take meals on the river-facing deck.
signature_address: Village Kalthar, Rishikesh-Badrinath Road, Shivpuri, Tehri-Garhwal 249192

name: Latitude (Aloha on the Ganges)
must_try: makki di roti with sarson ka saag
why_it_matters: The buffet restaurant inside Aloha on the Ganges, a 20,000-sq-yd Leisure Hotels resort opposite Rajaji National Park. Latitude is a Tripadvisor Travelers' Choice winner ranked top-10 in Rishikesh, with separate Jain and South Indian sections — rare at this scale in the city.
insider_tip: The Patio is the connected alfresco terrace facing the Ganga — order à la carte there for breakfast or sundowner snacks rather than the main buffet hall, which fills up with tour groups by 8pm.
signature_address: Village Shisham Jhadi, Muni Ki Reti, Tapovan, Rishikesh 249192

name: White Water Café (Atali Ganga)
signature_dish: rafter's set lunch overlooking the rapids
why_it_matters: Aquaterra Adventures' founder Vaibhav Kala built Atali Ganga in 2012 as the first proper boutique adventure resort in Rishikesh — 22 cottages on a 3-acre forested cliff above the Ganga at Mile 30. White Water Café is the in-house dining room; the menu is built for paddlers (carb-heavy lunches, big breakfasts) but presentation is plated, not buffet.
insider_tip: Outside guests can dine if they pre-arrange — the resort sits 38 km from Rishikesh on the Badrinath highway and isn't a casual drive-by. Ask for the deck table in monsoon when the rapids below run loudest.
signature_address: Milestone 30, Badrinath Road, Byasi, near Mohan Chatti, Rishikesh 249303

name: The Sitting Elephant (EllBee Ganga View)
why_it_matters: Rooftop restaurant of the EllBee Ganga View boutique hotel, with a clean line of sight to Triveni Ghat and the river. Strictly pure-veg, alcohol-free per Rishikesh bylaw. The vegan menu is genuinely worked-out, not a token afterthought — uncommon at this price point in town.
insider_tip: Time dinner with Triveni Ghat's 6:30pm Ganga aarti — the rooftop has a partial view of the lit ghats across the bend. Reserve a corner table on the river side; centre tables miss the angle.
signature_address: Hotel EllBee Ganga View, Haridwar Road, Manvendra Nagar, Rishikesh 249201

name: Jal Jalebi (Ganga Kinare)
why_it_matters: Ganga Kinare opened in 1989 as one of the few Rishikesh hotels built directly on the riverbank, with a private Ganga ghat. The flagship restaurant Jal Jalebi runs an Indian menu plus a rooftop and riverside terrace — pure-veg per local bylaw, no alcohol on premises.
insider_tip: The hotel arranges private candlelit dinners on its own ghat for an extra fee — book 24 hours ahead. The rooftop view points across to Rajaji National Park's southern flank.

name: Camp Aquaforest Dining
why_it_matters: One of the longer-running riverside camps registered with Uttarakhand Tourism, 9 km past Laxman Jhula in Shivpuri. Dining is package-bundled (breakfast + dinner buffet for in-camp guests), kitchen runs a fixed multi-cuisine menu rather than à la carte. Useful upscale-camp option in this zone where most Shivpuri camps default to canteen-grade food.
insider_tip: Day visitors generally can't drop in for meals — packages are stay-only. If you want the bonfire-dining experience without a full-night booking, ask whether they have a day-rafting + lunch combo at the time of the season.
signature_address: Shivpuri Beach, 9 km from Laxman Jhula, Rishikesh-Badrinath Road, Tehri-Garhwal 249192
